settings.title: Feeds

dialog.vulncheckKeySaved: A key ending in {{last4}} is saved. Leave empty to keep it.

dialog.vulncheckRemoveBody_other: Turns the feed off and deletes its list. {{n}} open findings came only from it.

They stay open, as when CISA drops a CVE: they keep their text, but their source information is no longer available. Close them yourself if they do not apply.
dialog.vulncheckRemoveConfirm: Remove key and delete the list

parser.title: How Vedette reads this feed
parser.intro: Choose the format, map each field, then test on a sample.
parser.introInfo: Choose the format, say where each field is, then test on a sample. Rows that do not fit are counted and skipped, never crash the fetch.
parser.recordsInfo: The JSONPath to the list of records. Supported: .key, ['key'], [n], [*].

note.json: Each record is mapped with a JSONPath relative to it, such as {{example}}.
note.csv: Name a column from the header, or give its number.
note.rss: Use item fields: title, link, description, pubDate (or published), category, id.
note.stix: Indicator objects are read; fields are fixed, nothing to map.
note.lines: One indicator per line; its kind is detected.

noteInfo.csv: Lines starting with # are skipped. Name a column from the header, or give its number.
noteInfo.stix: Vedette reads indicator objects and their patterns, such as [ipv4-addr:value = '203.0.113.7'], [domain-name:value = '...'], [url:value = '...'] and file hashes. A bundle or a TAXII collection response both work. Fields are fixed; nothing to map.
noteInfo.lines: One indicator per line; blank lines and # comments are skipped. Only the first word on each line is used. The kind (IP, domain, URL, hash) is detected.

parser.srcJson: JSONPath, for example {{example}}. Empty = not mapped.
parser.srcCsv: Column name or number. Empty = not mapped.
parser.regexHint: The first capture group is kept; no match rejects the row.
parser.ownPlaceholder: Paste a few lines of the feed here
parser.ownHint: Leave empty to use a built-in sample of this format.
parser.limits: Limits: {{size}} MB and {{rows}} rows per fetch.
parser.truncated: Stopped at the row limit ({{rows}}). Remaining rows would be ignored.
parser.noRecords: No records came out. Check the paths, column names or regex.
parser.firstRejectedLines: First rejected lines of the sample

tierCve.intro: This CVE is on no exploited list (CISA KEV, or VulnCheck KEV when it is on). Vedette lists the devices it confirmed under Recommended updates, grouped by the update that fixes it; it is never a finding and never alerts.
tierCve.introOld: This CVE is on no exploited list and was published more than 12 months ago, or this box has no NVD record of it. Vedette lists such a CVE on a device only when a scan engine finds it there.
tierCve.publishedNone: Not in the NVD data of the last 12 months
tierCve.epssNone: No EPSS score in the data
tierCve.rangesYes: NVD lists them, so Vedette can compare a device's exact version
tierCve.rangesNo: NVD has not listed them yet, so Vedette cannot compare a version (it never lists a CVE by the product name alone)
tierCve.noDevice: No device of yours is listed for it: Vedette found no confirmed version inside its affected versions.

dash.label: Today at a glance
dash.unchecked_one: You have 1 exploited CVE Vedette could not check on {{devices}} device: read it on the Findings page
dash.unchecked_other: You have {{count}} exploited CVEs Vedette could not check on {{devices}} devices: read them on the Findings page
dash.trendLabel: Open exploited findings over {{days}} days: {{first}} then, {{last}} now
dash.fixFirstInfo: The open findings that matter most: confirmed (by a scan, by the version the device itself reports, or by a person) before suspected, then those ransomware groups use, then the highest CVSS score, then the newest. Every one is on an exploited list (CISA KEV or VulnCheck KEV); CVSS says how bad the flaw is, not whether it is exploited.
dash.emptyTitle: Nothing you run is being exploited
dash.emptyBody_one: Vedette checks your {{count}} device again whenever the exploited lists change.
dash.emptyBody_other: Vedette checks your {{count}} devices again whenever the exploited lists change.
dash.emptyInfo: A finding appears here when a device runs a version listed as exploited in the wild (CISA KEV, VulnCheck KEV). Newly exploited vulnerabilities, matched or not, are on the board below.
